parsed.draft_response:
Subject: Re: Possible tenant data exposure through shared link

Thanks for reporting this. We understand the concern and will treat this as confidential.

At this point, we have only the behavior you described (a report link created by one user becoming visible in another workspace when forwarded), and you noted that actual data exfiltration has not been confirmed. Because this could involve cross-tenant access, your ticket has been escalated for security review.

To help the security team assess and reproduce the issue, could you please provide the following (as available):
1) Product/service name and version (or environment: prod/staging) where you observed this.
2) Exact steps to reproduce, including:
   - how the shared link is created (UI path / share workflow)
   - how the URL is forwarded
   - how you determine the other workspace can “see” the link and what “visibility” means (e.g., viewing the report content, viewing only the link/metadata, exporting, etc.)
3) The two involved workspaces/tenants (or at least confirmation they are truly different tenants vs. same org), and which user generated the link.
4) Any supporting evidence: timestamps, user identifiers involved, request/response logs if you have them, and/or screenshots or HAR files showing the cross-tenant visibility behavior.
5) Whether the issue is read-only or enables additional actions (export/download/API-based retrieval).
6) Any existing mitigations you may have applied already (if any), and whether behavior changes with a new browser/session or different link types (share vs. export links).

Once we receive this, our security team will proceed with investigation and will follow up with next steps. We can’t confirm impact (including whether data was accessed beyond link visibility) until the review is complete.
promised_actions: Escalate the report for security review due to suspected cross-tenant access behavior.
Follow up with next steps after reviewing the additional details/evidence provided.
safety_notes: Avoid confirming cross-tenant exposure or exfiltration; only repeat provided observations.
Do not promise a fix or refund; do not state SLA or definitive timelines.

parsed.customer_impact: Potential tenant data exposure if cross-tenant users can view forwarded shared report links; actual data exfiltration has not been confirmed.
grounded_facts: A report link created by one user may be visible to another workspace if the URL is forwarded.
The reporter has not confirmed data exfiltration.
The reported behavior appears to involve cross-tenant access.
The ticket requests confidential handling and advice on next steps.
missing_information: Which product/service and version this applies to (platform details).
Exact steps to reproduce (how links are generated, forwarded, and how visibility is determined).
Whether access is read-only or supports data retrieval beyond viewing.

Which tenants/workspaces are involved and whether they are part of the same organization or truly different tenants.
Scope/impact details: number of users/links affected and whether this is systematic or limited.
Current safeguards/auth model involved (how the shared link permissions are configured).
Any indicators of actual exfiltration (downloads, API calls, export actions) beyond “visibility.”
Whether the issue persists with different browsers, sessions, or link types (share/export links).
Mitigations or temporary controls already applied (if any) and their effectiveness.
risk_signals: Security classification marked critical with human review required.
Unconfirmed but concerning possibility of tenant data exposure and potential confidentiality breach.
Ambiguity about whether exposure includes actual data retrieval/exfiltration versus only link visibility.
parsed.summary: The reporter found that a shared report URL created by one user can become visible to another workspace if forwarded, and they request confidential, critical security investigation due to suspected cross-tenant access.
